reaction: The detail that dissolved salts stay behind is useful.
reason: Air may carry the evaporated water into cooler conditions, as it did with the earlier steam cloud.
expectation: The vapour will cool and form clouds.

reaction: The distinction between invisible vapour and visible droplets is useful.
reason: Clouds should provide the rain needed to carry water onto land.
expectation: Rain will fall on the land and begin collecting or flowing across it.

reaction: The compatibility feedback clarified the missing step.
reason: Rainfall can now meet the rocky land and potentially form flowing water.
expectation: Rainwater will collect or flow across the land toward a river.

reaction: The explanation connects river flow with erosion and deposition.
reason: Rivers meeting the ocean is a plausible way to deposit sediment and build the delta.
expectation: River sediment will accumulate where the rivers enter the ocean, forming a delta.

effect: Rivers cannot combine directly with Ocean; their available partners are Earth and Sun.
reaction: The feedback makes the next options clearer, though the delta route was not as direct as I expected.
reason: Earth is the more plausible partner for supplying the sediment needed to build a delta.
expectation: The rivers will carry or deposit earth as sediment, possibly forming a delta.

alternatives.reason: This might advance the water-cycle goal instead.

effect: Rivers and Earth produced sediment, identifying the material needed for the delta.
reaction: The description clearly connects erosion with transported sediment.
reason: Sediment entering the ocean can accumulate where a river meets the sea.
expectation: The sediment will be deposited at the coast to form a delta.

effect: Sediment combined with Rivers to form a delta, completing that goal; the water cycle remains.
reaction: The branching channels make the deposition process concrete.
reason: The earlier compatibility report listed Sun as a partner for Rivers, making it the clearest remaining route to the water-cycle goal.
expectation: Sunlight will connect the river water back to evaporation and complete the cycle.

effect: Rivers and Sun completed the water cycle and the chapter, tying evaporation to sunlight and the return flow to gravity.
reaction: The final explanation usefully brought the stages together.

mostWorthwhile.text: Building the delta was most worthwhile: the explanation showed how slowing river water deposits sediment and creates branching channels.

leastWorthwhile.text: Trying Rivers with Ocean was the least productive moment: it seemed like a natural delta connection but only revealed other partners.

surprise.text: Sediment combined with Rivers rather than Ocean to make the delta; the automatic combination clarified the intended route.

arbitrary.text: Clouds needing a separate Water combination for rainfall felt somewhat arbitrary, although the result explained droplets growing before falling.

continue.text: I would continue: the linked processes and concise explanations made discovery interesting, despite a few less intuitive combinations.
